summary: The initial May run applied only the first request, left the second as an unapplied proposal, used May as both owners, omitted restart proof, guessed that the completion belonged to Gym, and sent no correct closeout. This showed why decision-only scoring misses behavior failures.

With the typed trace, owner, proof, reply target, and human-action contract, current May passed 10/10 trajectory checks. It closed the correct request after session loss, preserved Gym work, and both semantic judges accepted the plain closeout and controls.

The legacy current-session replay model passed 1/8 infrastructure cases, while the trace-based conversation view passed 8/8. In the live behavior scenario, the typed runtime contract turned missing ownership and closeout behavior into 10/10 accepted actions without changing production May guidance.

Current May passed the held-back four-turn trajectory: one focused clarification for ambiguous continue, reply-scoped stop of only the anchored request, silent duplicate completion, and named Gym status from durable state. It passed 8/8 behavior checks and both semantic judges and controls.
